hints.title: Sublist Boundary Reconnection Obstacle
hints.text: Reversing the entire list alters untouched prefixes and suffixes. How can you navigate directly to the left boundary and rewire internal links while retaining external connections?

hints.title: Head-Insertion Sub-segment Inversion Invariant
hints.text: Advance to the node preceding left, then iteratively move each subsequent node in the range [left, right] to the front of the reversed sub-segment.

hints.title: Repeated Head Shift Procedure
hints.text: Use a dummy head and advance prev to position left - 1. Set curr to prev.next. For right - left iterations, extract curr.next, insert it immediately after prev, and update curr.next to point to the following node. Return dummy.next.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def reverseBetween(self, head: Optional[ListNode], left: int, right: int) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        if not head or left == right:
            return head
        dummy = ListNode(0, head)
        prev = dummy
        for _ in range(left - 1):
            prev = prev.next
        curr = prev.next
        for _ in range(right - left):
            nxt = curr.next
            curr.next = nxt.next
            nxt.next = prev.next
            prev.next = nxt
        return dummy.next
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (1 <= N <= 500)
left, right: indices (1 <= left <= right <= N)
complexity.notes: Single pass advancing to left and performing right - left head shifts in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Multi-pass approaches traversing once to isolate nodes and once to stitch add unnecessary overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place link splicing requires O(1) auxiliary space and exactly one traversal pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clean one-pass pointer manipulation without off-by-one errors when left = 1.
